JPM.rationale: JPMorgan Chase demonstrates strong fundamental health and positive trajectory. Q1 2026 showed revenue of $49.84B (+10% YoY) and EPS of $5.94 (+17.2% YoY), with sequential acceleration across all metrics. The Q2 2026 earnings report (July 14) was exceptional: record net income of $21.2B, revenue of $57.3B (+28% YoY), and EPS of $7.70 crushing estimates by 38.7%. Every business line posted record revenue, with equity markets revenue surging 86% and investment banking fees up 30%. The bank raised full-year NII guidance to $105.5B. ROE of 16.2% and net margins of 31.5% reflect durable profitability. The balance sheet is massive ($4.9T assets) with $375B equity, and the bank passed stress tests with a 14.3% tier 1 capital ratio, enabling a $50B buyback authorization and 10% dividend increase. JPM holds #1 global ranking in investment banking fees (8.4% share) and manages $5T+ in AUM. Valuation is moderate: P/E of 15.8x sits mid-range of its 13.7-17.8x 1-year range, while P/B of 2.56x is near the upper end of its 2.2-2.8x range. The stock has risen 12.2% over the past quarter to $343, near its 52-week high of $351.24, which limits upside from current levels. The Epstein-related regulatory/reputational risk around CEO Dimon (Senator Warren inquiry due July 24, Jes Staley interview July 23) introduces unquantifiable near-term downside risk that partially offsets the strong fundamentals. Macro backdrop is mixed: Fed funds at 3.63% supports NII, but 10Y yield at 4.57% and rising could pressure valuations; VIX at 16.7 is moderate. News sentiment is positive (mean 0.35 over 90 days). The score reflects excellent fundamentals and trajectory offset by near-full valuation and episodic regulatory risk.
